measured: the products volter.ai names and the open-source applications in scope, read in the demand scan's clones (~/.cache/twin-demand) at the commits below (twin-world generated/demand.json). Open Autonomy's backend is the one caller of Gateway's model surfaces: its model rail (packages/backend/src/proxy.ts) forwards each model call a stock OpenAI or Anthropic SDK makes to it, with its own key (MODEL_GATEWAY_API_KEY) as a bearer token and a bare model id mapped to openai/ or anthropic/; it reads usage (usage.cost on the OpenAI surfaces, routing.merge_fee_usd) to settle the account, streamed or not, and turns a 4xx into provider_rejected_request, a 401/403 into upstream_auth_failed, a 429 into provider_rate_limited; its /v1/catalog route pages Gateway's GET /v1/models by next_cursor (routes.ts:315). The request carries no originator or X-Merge-Wire-Format header, so /v1/responses answers Merge's native shape. RH2, Volter Harness and Substrate reach Gateway through that rail: each carries the Open Autonomy kit whose Hermes worker calls chat completions on zai/glm-5.3-flash through the host valve. Substrate's Volter Editor page (examples/volter-editor, the published @browser-substrate/volter-editor) also calls Gateway directly: Pi's provider is the page's loopback port, which adds the vault's key and relays each request to api-gateway.merge.dev (openai-completions, anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). No other listed application names Gateway, MODEL_GATEWAY_URL or api-gateway.merge.dev; Open Autonomy's apps/platform/world.ts and test/env.ts are a World and a test, not demand.
